replayed.description: True when this acceptance had already happened and the same cart version is being returned.

occurrence_key.description: The deterministic identity of one scheduled moment: the local wall-clock time plus its zone. Derived only from the schedule, so a retry, a replay, a restart and a duplicate scheduler delivery all present the same key and collide on a unique index rather than creating a second generation.

state.description: AUTO_APPROVED means the occurrence is inside the bounded preauthorization the customer themselves configured. It creates no order and moves no money.

address_ref.description: The customer's OWN saved-location reference. Raw coordinates are deliberately not accepted: pricing a delivery to an address the caller has no connection to would leak serviceability information about arbitrary points on the map.

budget_minor.description: A ceiling on the FINAL DELIVERED total. Omit for no budget.

PlanComparison.description: SAME_VENDOR versus OPTIMIZED, both priced against TODAY's catalogue. The same-vendor side is not last week's receipt: a customer deciding whether to accept a change needs to know what declining it would cost now.

quoted_available_quantity.description: Stock AT THE TIME OF QUOTING. Named for what it is: nothing here reserved it, and checkout revalidates it.

Requirement.description: One thing the customer needs. A requirement is a NEED, not a SKU: 'two litres of permitted milk' survives a vendor going out of stock, changing price or leaving the platform, and 'listing lst_9f21 x2' does not.

category_ref.description: A canonical taxonomy node, for a need stated as a need rather than as a product. This is what lets a recurring basket re-shop instead of re-buying a decision made months ago.

minimum_quality_grade.description: HARD. Checkable because the catalogue states which grades a listing offers. Note the asymmetry with the QUALITY_BALANCED objective: a stated grade requirement is checkable, and RANKING two listings by quality is not, because the platform holds no ordinal quality signal.

preferred_brands.description: SOFT. Breaks ties among candidates that already satisfy every hard constraint.

quantity.description: Satisfied exactly or reported as unmet. A cheaper basket is never produced by quietly delivering fewer items.

required_brand.description: HARD. No objective, no budget shortfall and no saving may set it aside; a cheaper substitute of another brand is not offered at any price.

substitution.description:
Defaults to EXACT_ONLY. The most restrictive value is the default on purpose: a customer who said nothing about substitution has not consented to any.

SAME_PRODUCT_ANY_VENDOR is barely a substitution - the same manufactured article bought at a different shop. EQUIVALENT_PRODUCT additionally permits a different product the taxonomy authority maps to the same canonical node, subject to brand and quality constraints.

Nothing is ever substituted on name similarity. Equivalence comes from a manufacturer trade identifier, the catalogue product identity or the taxonomy authority - never from two products sounding alike.

minimum_feasible_delivered_total_minor.description: The cheapest COMPLETE basket satisfying every hard constraint, whatever it costs. Computed from real candidates, and absent when no complete basket exists - quoting a price for something that cannot be bought would be worse than saying nothing.

no_complete_basket.description: At least one requirement cannot be satisfied at ANY price. A different answer from 'too expensive', and kept apart from it.

optimality_note.description: The exact claim this API makes. Not 'the cheapest basket': the search is bounded, so for most inputs some baskets were never looked at, and a stronger word would be a stronger claim than the implementation supports.

quality_variant_unavailable_reason.description: Why no QUALITY_BALANCED variant was produced. The platform holds a quality-grade SELECTION vocabulary for fresh goods and no ordinal quality score for anything, so for most requests this variant genuinely cannot be produced - and inventing a score to fill the slot would be presenting a fabrication as advice.

search_truncated.description: A configured bound stopped the search before every candidate basket was evaluated. Reported rather than hidden: an optimizer that silently truncates and presents its answer as the best available is claiming a thoroughness it does not have.

equivalence_basis.description: The authority that says these two are interchangeable. There is deliberately no value meaning 'the names looked similar'.

approval_policy.description:
Defaults to ALWAYS_ASK. Silence is not consent.

AUTO_VENDOR_CHANGE_WITHIN_CEILING permits a VENDOR change for the SAME product, within the ceiling - the article is unchanged, so the customer receives exactly what they chose from a different shop. No policy permits a different product, a different brand, an unmet quantity or a material price rise without asking.

day_of_month.description: Capped at 28: a monthly basket that silently skipped February would recur less often than the customer was told.

delivery_total_minor.description: Priced by the quote-only fulfilment planner against real logistics quotes. It is never estimated as a fixed fee per vendor, because delivery is most of the difference between two baskets of the same groceries and a made-up fee would decide the comparison.

final_delivered_total_minor.description: The only number the customer pays, and the only one a budget is evaluated against.

proposal_id.description: Present when this variant was persisted as an acceptable offer.

Funding.description: customer + vendor + platform always equals gross, enforced by the database. It is what keeps 'who actually paid for this delivery' answerable at settlement.

candidates.description: Every alternative considered, selected and rejected alike. Keeping the losers is the point: a plan that stored only the winner cannot answer why the other option was not chosen.

mode.description: The preference this plan was optimized for. It flows unchanged into the CheckoutQuote as selected_fulfilment_mode, so a plan quoted as SAVER cannot later be executed as FASTEST against a charge the customer never approved.

optimization_policy_version.description: The threshold envelope the comparison was decided under. Thresholds move; an explanation that silently re-read today's numbers would have stopped explaining what happened.

completion_minutes.description: Time to the LAST delivery. Parallel legs overlap, so this is not the sum of the legs.

detour_minutes.description: How much longer this candidate's slowest leg is than the slowest leg of the fully split alternative. Measured against the split alternative's own QUOTED transit, not against an estimate - which is why both alternatives are priced before either is compared.

service_capabilities.description: Which logistics authorities could drive a multi-stop collection at the moment of the decision. Without it, reading MULTI_STOP_UNSUPPORTED back in a year would be an assertion with nothing behind it.

status.description: INELIGIBLE is not REJECTED. A candidate refused by a safety or capability constraint was never a real option, and recording it as rejected-on-price would suggest the optimizer weighed safety against money. The database refuses to store a constraint reason on any other status.

fulfilment_preference.description:
FASTEST minimises time to the last delivery and may choose parallel missions even when consolidation would be cheaper. BALANCED is the default trade-off. SAVER minimises what the customer pays, inside the wider delivery window they accepted.

No mode may override a safety or service constraint. A capacity limit, a temperature rule, a fragile load, a closed handover window, a promised arrival time or a missing runtime capability refuses a consolidation in every mode, and the refusal is recorded as INELIGIBLE rather than as a price decision.

CampaignObjective.description: All five are marketing objectives and all five evaluate against the single consent purpose MARKETING. CampaignChannel.description: The Section 8A consent channels and nothing else. A channel outside this set could never have a consent decision projected for it, so a campaign naming one could never lawfully target it.

SnapshotStatus.description: BUILDING covers queued, running and awaiting-retry: the audience is not current and preparation is still trying. FAILED means it stopped trying. Neither ever disturbs the previous CURRENT snapshot, and a partial audience can never become CURRENT.

SnapshotEligibilityState.description: Two values, not five. SuppressionReasonCode.description: Why a target stopped being actionable AFTER its snapshot was frozen. These never rewrite the snapshot; they sit beside it.

PreviewReasonCode.description: Deliberately coarse categories that explain an outcome to vendor staff without disclosing the consent authority's reasoning, the underlying query, or anything about the customer.

ExperimentVariant.description: One cohort. Allocation is in integer basis points; there is no percentage field and no floating point, because an allocation that does not sum exactly is an experiment whose control group silently changes size between runs.

FrequencyPolicy.description: Stored and versioned here, enforced only at send time. evaluation_state is always NOT_AVAILABLE because no campaign has been delivered and there is no contact history to count against; an empty history would make every cap pass, which would be the most misleading possible answer.

QuietHoursPolicy.description: Minute-of-day plus a mandatory IANA zone, so a cross-midnight window (22:00 -> 07:00) is unambiguous. Section 8E schedules nothing; would_block is returned only when a caller supplies an explicit hypothetical instant, and enforcement is Section 8F's.

service_recovery_suppression_enabled.description: Defaults to true. Marketing to a customer in the middle of an unresolved complaint is the failure this exists to prevent, so opting out has to be a deliberate choice.

experiment_variants.description: At most one control (<= 5000 bps) and one to five treatment variants. Allocations must total exactly 10000 basis points.

hypothetical_send_at.description: Asks the quiet-hours question for one instant. It schedules nothing; Section 8E has no scheduler.

operation.description:
Atomically replaces the whole ladder. Replacement rather than per-rung editing is deliberate: a ladder is only valid as a set, so an operation that moved one rung would have to either reject most edits or accept a transiently invalid ladder. Every write is therefore a transition between two valid states.

Ranks are DERIVED from the thresholds and must not be supplied; a caller-supplied rank could disagree with its own threshold ordering and the ladder would then have two answers to which tier is higher. Thresholds must be distinct - two rungs at the same entry point make membership ambiguous, and an ambiguous customer-facing status is worse than having no tiers at all. At most 8 tiers.

Superseded rungs are archived, not deleted, so an audit record that referenced a tier keeps something to point at. Segments that read a loyalty field are invalidated in the same transaction, because their materialised membership was computed against the old ladder.
